attributes.title: Level 5

subgroups.name: Discover

steps.text: Watch this video to learn about defining your own functions, with and without parameters of different types, to create code that can be called throughout your project.

questions.hint: What type of code only runs when it is called?
questions.title: [Select one] A(n) _________________ is a chunk of code that runs whenever it’s called.
questions.correctResponse: A function is a chunk of code that runs whenever it’s called. Functions make it easier to reuse a chunk of code multiple times in a project.

questions.hint: What type of parameter is defined in the callLevel function definition?
questions.title: [Select one] In this function, what type of argument will the function’s parameter accept?
questions.correctResponse: Parameters may be declared by typing the name of the parameter, a colon :, and the type of parameter it will be.

questions.hint: What do number, string, and image variable arguments look like in JavaScript?
questions.title: [Match one per answer] Match the function call to the correct function parameter types:
questions.correctResponse: Parameters can make functions even more powerful, because they allow you to change the arguments that get passed to the function. In this example, the makePizza function is called with different arguments, based on the parameter types in the function definition.

questions.hint: Will a function’s code run if it is only defined in a project?
questions.title: [Select one] The code inside a function will not run unless the function has been called.
questions.correctResponse: A function will only run if the function has been called.

questions.hint: What symbols surround a function’s code?
questions.title: [Select one] Code inside of a function’s definition cannot be accessed by any other part of the project.
questions.correctResponse: A function’s code is surrounded by a pair of curly brackets { }, which prevents its code from being accessed by any other part of the project.

questions.hint: What symbols should be used to add a documentation box comment?
questions.title: [Select one] Which comment will add text to a function’s documentation box?

answers.text: // create Enemy sprites and place in random positions
create Enemy sprites and place in random positions
/** * create Enemy sprites and place in random positions          */
/* create Enemy sprites and place in random positions */

questions.correctResponse: By starting a comment with /** and ending it with */, the comment will be added to the documentation box and will appear whenever the cursor hovers over the function name.

subgroups.title: Functions!
subgroups.introduction: Watch this video to learn about defining your own functions, with and without parameters of different types, to create code that can be called throughout your project.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 5 of Purple Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about functions. Functions can be used to name a unique chunk of code that can be easily reused in a project. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 5:

badges.title: Function Junction
badges.description: Create and call functions that use different parameter types in JavaScript.

badges.title: Functional Thinking
badges.description: Create a new function, with or without parameters, in JavaScript.

badges.title: Calling All Functions
badges.description: Call a function, with or without parameters, in JavaScript.

badges.title: Time for a Change
badges.description: Change the border color of the countdown timer.

badges.title: Feeling Shifty
badges.description: Use the shift function to remove and return the first value in an array.

badges.title: Read the Manual
badges.description: Use a block comment to document a function.

badges.title: Free Fallin’
badges.description: Set the acceleration of a sprite to simulate gravity.
